_comment: What a P value does and does not say: chance only, never the design and never causation.

stem.en: Table 12 reports P < 0.001 for the gap between the two exposure rates. Which reading of that value is correct?

text.en: There is a 0.1 per cent chance that smoking caused the lung cancer in these men
A gap this big would be very unlikely if smoking and lung cancer had no link, and the value says nothing about how the men were chosen or asked
The result proves that smoking causes lung cancer in 99.9 per cent of smokers
The same gap would appear in any population, because a value this small cannot come from chance

explanation.en: P is the chance of a gap this large if smoking and lung cancer had no link, so a small value means chance is an unlikely explanation. It is not the chance that smoking caused the cancer, and it cannot detect a problem in the way the cases and controls were selected or questioned.

hints.en: Ask what the shuffles in the scene can change and what they leave exactly as it was.
